conclusions: Known useful-success at 10 lower bound rises from 1/16 to 3/16; wide incomplete-judgment bounds overlap, so no global semantic quality/noise winner.
Added-token exposure measures intervention reach, not semantic badness. No new judged-negative labels were invented.
Frequency3 improves fictional-name completion but regresses gish-reference to two cold and one reuse-attempt timeout.
Names80 generates and correctly orders Red Raphael, but it ranks 11th in its word-count bucket, outside the default ten-row limit. Vocabulary coverage is necessary, not sufficient.
136 successful cold/reuse pairs hit and preserve buckets; one nominal reuse after cold failure completes without a cache hit.
Fresh compiled CLI baseline buckets match all 22 successful earlier public capture samples despite differing executable hashes.
No experimental corpus or ranker weights promoted. Broader contextual human labeling remains required.
